summary: 22270875 (15 double-blind placebo-controlled trials, 360 mostly young active adults, 2.4-6.4 g/day) found a positive overall effect on exercise measures (P=0.002), driven by exercise capacity and efforts of 60 s or longer, with no effect on performance tests or efforts under 60 s. Dr. Pham's hold was a date restriction whose age-only exclusion was withdrawn; the source meets the credit rules for an exercise-capacity scope. The newer 27797728 agrees (ES 0.18) but is abstract-only. Fourth-ruling boundary applied: repeated-use high-intensity exercise only, with a 2.4 g/day studied-range floor so single small servings do not inherit credit; outcome hierarchy not_reported.

applicability.studied_population: Healthy, mostly young active adults taking 2.4-6.4 g/day beta-alanine daily for several weeks (repeated-use protocols); benefit is high-intensity exercise capacity, not a single pre-workout serving or general energy.
applicability.reason: 2026-10-28 fourth-ruling boundary: credit only for repeated-use (weeks) protocols at studied daily amounts; the 2.4 g/day minimum is the lowest studied daily dose in 22270875 (correspondence to the tested range, not an efficacy threshold).

identity.preparation: Chronic oral beta-alanine alone versus placebo (beta-alanine-only arms; co-supplement arms excluded)

population.description: 15 placebo-controlled double-blind trials, 360 participants (174 beta-alanine, 186 placebo); 77.2% young healthy active males, 20.3% female, 7.2% aged 55-92.

study_contexts.study_design: Meta-analysis of double-blind placebo-controlled human trials with a beta-alanine-only arm; 57 effect sizes from 23 exercise tests; median effect sizes compared.

outcomes.name: All exercise measures: beta-alanine median ES 0.374 (IQR 0.140-0.747) vs placebo 0.108 (-0.019 to 0.487), P=0.002; median improvement 2.85%
Exercise capacity improved (P=0.013); exercise performance not improved (P=0.204)
By duration: 60-240 s improved (P=0.001), >240 s improved (P=0.046), <60 s no benefit (P=0.312)

limitations: Small trials (7-20 per group), mostly young active men; capacity tests benefited while time-trial performance did not; effects are modest (2.85% median).
Paraesthesia may unblind participants (Discussion). Five studies acknowledged commercial financial support; eight received donated supplement.
No dose-response relationship was found (P=0.337); 2.4-6.4 g/day is the studied range, not a minimum.

Declared 27797728 (40 studies, 1461 participants, overall ES 0.18, 95% CI 0.08-0.28; benefit concentrated in 0.5-10 min exercise capacity) has no open full text; inspected at abstract level and supplies no separate context.
Supports high-intensity exercise capacity/muscular endurance only; not general energy or fatigue outside exercise.

freshness_search.screening_rule: Restricted to syntheses, because beta-alanine has dozens of small RCTs that the syntheses pool. Kept syntheses of beta-alanine alone on exercise outcomes. Excluded co-supplementation-only, sport-specific multi-supplement network MAs without a beta-alanine-alone estimate, carnosine and cognition reviews, and protocols.

read.title: Effect of Beta-Alanine Supplementation on Maximal Intensity Exercise in Trained Young Male Individuals: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
read.finding: 2024 SR/MA, 18 double-blind RCTs, 331 trained men aged 18-40, chronic dosing: maximal efforts of 0.5-10 min ES 0.39 (0.09 to 0.69); 4-10 min efforts ES 0.55; 5.6-6.4 g/day ES 0.35; significant from 4 weeks.

read.title: Effects of beta-alanine supplementation on exercise performance and related physiological outcomes in women: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
read.finding: 2026 SR/MA in women, 11 RCTs (312): time to exhaustion SMD 0.49 (0.20 to 0.79). Other outcomes were imprecise, and certainty was very low.

read.title: No ergogeniceffect of β-alanine on repeated sprint ability: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
read.finding: 2026 multilevel MA, 17 RCTs (at least 2 weeks of dosing): no effect on mean or peak repeated-sprint performance or fatigue decrement, regardless of dose, duration or training status.

read.title: Effects of Beta-Alanine Supplementation on Physical Performance in Aerobic-Anaerobic Transition Zones: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
read.finding: 2020 MA, 19 studies: small effects in aerobic-anaerobic transition zones. Only one acute-dosing study exists.

read.title: Beta-Alanine for Improving Exercise Capacity, Muscle Strength, and Functional Performance of Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
read.finding: 2025 SR of 5 trials in older adults (163; 2.4-3.2 g/day for about 12 weeks): exercise capacity may improve; strength and functional performance do not.

freshness_search.conclusion: confirms: newer syntheses agree with 22270875. The benefit is for sustained high-intensity efforts (about 0.5-10 min; time to exhaustion) after weeks of 2.4-6.4 g/day, with none for repeated short sprints or strength. The existing repeated-use, high-intensity-capacity scope and the 2.4 g/day floor fit this evidence.

integration_notes: 2026-10-28 integrator: excluded_claim_terms ['energy','focus','pre-workout energy'] removed. _excluded_claim_matches scans the whole label, so a correctly dosed product (Tri-Phase, 3.2 g/day) lost credit over the phrase 'target the body's energy systems'. The ruling's single-serving boundary is enforced by the 2.4 g/day minimum.
